title: Account Usage API
summary: Retrieve your account usage and plan limits directly from the API.
body_markdown:
Today, we're introducing the[Usage API](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/usage/retrieve-usage) . One request returns your current usage and limits across every quota on your account.


## What you can build with it


- **Quota alerts** : notify your team before you hit your daily or monthly email limit.
- **Send throttling** : pause non-critical sends when you're close to a cap.
- **Internal dashboards** : show Resend usage next to your infrastructure metrics.
- **Agent awareness** : let your agent check remaining quota.


## Retrieving your usage


Call[GET /usage](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/usage/retrieve-usage) with a[full access](https://resend.com/changelog/new-api-key-permissions) API key.


```text
import     {   Resend   }     from     'resend'  ;
const   resend   =     new     Resend  (  're_xxxxxxxxx'  )  ;
const     {   data  ,   error   }     =     await   resend  .  usage  .  get  (  )  ;


```


## What's in the response


The response covers every quota on your account:


- **` emails`** : sent and received emails, viewable by` daily` or` monthly` windows.
- **` contacts`** : how many contacts have been used from your quota.
- **` segments`** : how many segments have been used from your quota (if applicable).
- **` broadcasts`** : how many total broadcasts have been created.
- **` domains`** : how many domains have been used from your quota (if applicable).
- **` ai_credits`** : credits used along with` next_increase_at` .
- **` automation_runs`** : runs used this period and when the count resets.
- **` rate_limit`** : your team's API rate limit for all requests.


A` limit` of` null` means there's no cap for that resource on your plan.


```text
{        "object"  :     "usage"  ,        "emails"  :     {          "daily"  :     {            "used"  :     10  ,            "limit"  :     100  ,            "sent"  :     8  ,            "received"  :     2  ,            "resets_at"  :     "2026-07-29T00:00:00.000Z"          }  ,          "monthly"  :     {            "used"  :     100  ,            "limit"  :     3000  ,            "sent"  :     80  ,            "received"  :     20  ,            "resets_at"  :     "2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z"          }        }  ,        "contacts"  :     {          "used"  :     10  ,          "limit"  :     3000        }  ,        "segments"  :     {          "used"  :     1  ,          "limit"  :     3        }  ,        "broadcasts"  :     {          "used"  :     2  ,          "limit"  :     null        }  ,        "ai_credits"  :     {          "used"  :     5  ,          "limit"  :     100  ,          "next_increase_at"  :     null        }  ,        "automation_runs"  :     {          "used"  :     3  ,          "limit"  :     10000  ,          "resets_at"  :     "2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z"        }  ,        "domains"  :     {          "used"  :     1  ,          "limit"  :     1        }  ,        "rate_limit"  :     {          "limit"  :     1000  ,          "duration"  :     "1000ms"        }     }
```


## Available in the CLI and MCP server


Run` resend usage` in the[CLI](https://resend.com/docs/cli) to see a table of your usage, or` resend usage --json` for scripts. The[MCP server](https://resend.com/docs/mcp-server) also includes a` get-usage` tool, so your agent can check your limits on its own.


To learn more, check out the[API documentation](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/usage/retrieve-usage) .
